newsitem.title: UK: ALUMINIUM AND ZINC LEAD GAINS ON LME PRE-MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ALUMINIUM AND ZINC LEAD GAINS ON LME PRE-MARKET.

text.p: Aluminium prices broke upwards to a new 22-month high during Thursday LME pre-market trading, and with zinc also strong the complex was largely displaying a steadier sheen, traders said.
Aluminium moved early and hit the $1,750 chart resistance target, subsequently triggering buy-stops. Stocks were down again - dropping by 1,400 tonnes.
Although the market is still overbought, and most of the buying is speculative, there is further scope on the upside in the short-term.
"People think it can go to $1,775, so those who want to sell are holding off," one trader said.
Prices touched $1,762 a tonne before settling at $1,760, up $18.50 from Wednesday's kerb. The cash/threes backwardation was widening out slightly to $7/10.
Similar action was seen in zinc, with the market skipping up from early little changed levels to touch $1,550.
There was little fresh behind the move, with the market still being buttressed by concerns over Chinese short positions and the September tightness. The overall cash/threes spread was at $105/115.
Three months prices were trading at $1,545 a tonne, a $17 gain from the previous kerb.
Copper was massaged by the general trend, and was able to push back above $2,300, although conditions were not active and the market needs to clear resistance at $2,310, traders said.
Stocks rose by 800 tonnes, although this had little impact.
"These are being discounted now - they are going up all the time," another trader said.
Three months was trading at $2,309, up $11 from the overnight close.
Elsewhere, lead took advantage of zinc's strength and sought to establish some distance from recent lows under $600. Prices were $9 higher at $615.
Nickel fluctuated on the pre-market, slopping lower to $7,165 at one point before clawing back some of the ground lost on Wednesday.

Prices were $50 higher at $7,210, although the upside is restricted with inventories in an uptrend. Stocks rose 294 tonnes on Thursday. Tin and alloy were neglected, but indicated at levels of $5,590/5,600 and $1,547/1,557. --Martin Hayes, London Newsroom 44 171 542 8080
